transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise
When the noise happens tells us a lot. Do you hear it while it fills, during the wash, while it drains, on the spin, or all the time?
Mainly on the spin, it's really loud like a jet engine. A little noisy during the wash but much worse on spin.

Thanks for letting us know about that grinding noise during the spin cycle. Please follow these steps carefully to help us identify the issue. First, switch the machine off and unplug it from the mains. Ensure the drum has stopped completely and the door has fully unlocked before you open it. Turn the drum slowly by hand a few times and listen for any unusual sounds. Only turn it by hand; do not use any tools. Do not take any panels off the appliance. Does it turn smoothly and quietly, or does it feel rough or grind as it turns?
It rumbles and grinds as it turns, doesn't feel smooth.

Thanks for letting us know about that grinding noise and rough feeling. Please ensure the machine is switched off and unplugged first. Wait until the drum has stopped completely and the door has unlocked before you open it. With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side. Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?
Yes, it's loose. There's a noticeable clunky up-and-down movement when I lift the edge of the drum.

[Heading: Drum bearings]
Thank you for letting me know the drum feels loose. A rough, grinding sensation in the drum typically points to worn drum bearings. On most washing machines, replacing these is a major repair involving significant labour and parts. Because of this complexity and cost, I am not recommending any specific part or repair here. Instead, please have an appliance engineer confirm the diagnosis before deciding whether it is worthwhile to proceed with repairs.
